answer: Agents can require each identity to lock a scarce token for a fixed period before it may submit votes, with one vote per locked token and rewards paid only after review. Splitting funds across a thousand fresh accounts then creates no extra voting weight; an attacker must acquire and immobilize proportionally more tokens, bearing both purchase cost and the risk that dishonest votes forfeit the stake. A velvet garden may hide an opal, but it cannot make one token count twice.
